note: Opened with curl on 15 October 2026 (200, full text in the page). Title exact. Byline Sumedha Mittal and Ayushi Kar, edited by Nitin Sethi; free to read. The visible date and 'Published on' are 14 October 2026; the page's JSON-LD says datePublished and dateModified 'Oct 13, 2026', probably a time-zone artefact, so 2026-10-14 is kept. All five quotations are verbatim. Corrected one point in 'shows': the article says Rinwa answered on X 'minutes after' the 9 October report, calling it riddled with 'falsehoods and inaccuracies', and that the same evening he posted a video calling it a 'misleading report'. So the word 'misleading' belongs to the video, and IANS's report of a post calling the claim 'भ्रामक' (misleading) is dated Tuesday 13 October. 'Did not dispute the count' is a fair plain reading of the paper's 'confirmed our finding', which rests on what he did not say. The 4,700 among 13.39 crore is his, as the paper quotes him. The cap: the body says the Commission ordered on 9 October that no person may file more than 30 objections a month, and the subheading says 'Two days later'. PTI (ThePrint, dateline New Delhi, Oct 9), News On AIR (10 Oct) and Deccan Herald, Deccan Chronicle, DT Next and Outlook all give 10 Form 7s per elector in the claims and objections period and five a month in continuous updation. None of them prints the letter, so none is primary, but the 30 is the Collective's alone, and 'shows' rightly gives no number. 'shows' names no private person, says nothing on religion beyond the title, and passes the writing rules. Group 'Investigations' fits.

fix.shows: A follow-up to the Collective's investigation of 9 October 2026 into the 85,854 Form 7s that the Commission's software ERONET produced in Uttar Pradesh with no reason for deletion. It reports that the state's Chief Electoral Officer answered on X within minutes, calling the report false, and that evening called it misleading in a recorded video, in which he did not dispute the count or explain why the reasons were missing. It quotes him putting the names targeted by bulk Form 7s at about 4,700 among 13.39 crore electors, and reports that the Commission capped the number of deletion objections one person may file.

fix.shows: A lawyer's essay for an international readership on the protests in Delhi on 10 and 12 October 2026 and how the SIR reached them. It argues that the Supreme Court let the revision become a fact on the ground before ruling on it, then upheld it in 2026 and, in the author's view, freed the Commission from having to act proportionately, and that the Commission's independence was never secured in law. It cites the 90% of decided West Bengal appeals that restored the elector and the Indian Express investigation into the two Commissioners' objections.
